candidates.primary_query: darf man mit dem roller auf die autobahn vietnam
candidates.intent_rationale: Riders planning trips out of Hanoi see expressways in navigation apps and need to know that motorbikes may not use them, and what entering one costs, before choosing a route.
candidates.content_angle: Explains Article 25(3) of Law 36/2024/QH15 excluding motorbikes and mopeds from expressways, the Decree 168/2024 fine for entering one, how to recognise expressway entrances and plan routes on roads open to motorbikes.
candidates.working_title: Mit dem Roller auf die Autobahn? Warum Schnellstraßen in Vietnam tabu sind

references.title: Consolidated text of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety (Law 36/2024/QH15), Government portal (Article 25(3))
Government policy portal: full text of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP on road traffic administrative penalties (Article 7(7)(b), entering an expressway)

candidates.primary_query: wie viele personen auf einem roller vietnam erlaubt
secondary_queries: zu dritt roller fahren vietnam strafe
kind auf dem roller vietnam regeln
candidates.intent_rationale: Couples, families and groups want to know how many people may ride one motorbike in Vietnam, and whether children count, before deciding how many bikes to rent.
candidates.content_angle: Explains Article 33(1) of Law 36/2024/QH15: one passenger as the rule, at most two only for a sick person going to emergency care, a person under arrest, a child under 12 or an elderly or disabled person; helmet duties for everyone on board; and the Decree 168/2024 fine for carrying two passengers outside those cases.
candidates.working_title: Wie viele Personen dürfen in Vietnam auf einem Roller sitzen?

references.title: Consolidated text of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety (Law 36/2024/QH15), Government portal (Article 33(1))
Government policy portal: full text of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP on road traffic administrative penalties (Article 7(2)(g), carrying two passengers)

candidates.primary_query: überholen mit dem roller vietnam regeln
candidates.intent_rationale: Riders coming from countries with different overtaking habits want to know on which side Vietnamese law allows overtaking, where it is banned and how to signal it, before riding out of the city.
candidates.content_angle: Explains Article 14 of Law 36/2024/QH15: overtake on the left, on the right only when the vehicle ahead is turning left, the places where overtaking is banned (narrow bridges, blind bends and crests, junctions, rail crossings, pedestrian crossings, tunnels), signalling with lights only at night in towns, and the Decree 168/2024 fines.
candidates.working_title: Überholen mit dem Roller in Vietnam: links, rechts und wo es verboten ist

references.title: Consolidated text of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety (Law 36/2024/QH15), Government portal (Article 14)
Government policy portal: full text of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP on road traffic administrative penalties (Article 7(1)(b) and 7(3)(đ), overtaking)

candidates.primary_query: wenden mit dem roller vietnam wo verboten
candidates.intent_rationale: Visitors find U-turns and left turns in Vietnamese traffic confusing and want to know where turning around is banned and how to signal it before riding a rental bike.
candidates.content_angle: Explains Article 15 of Law 36/2024/QH15: signalling and moving into the nearest lane before turning, giving way to pedestrians and oncoming traffic, the places where U-turns are banned (pedestrian crossings, bridges, under overpasses, narrow or steep roads, blind bends, one-way streets, tunnels, expressways), and the Decree 168/2024 fine.
candidates.working_title: Wenden und Abbiegen mit dem Roller in Vietnam: Wo es verboten ist

Government policy portal: full text of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP on road traffic administrative penalties (Article 7(2)(k), U-turns where not allowed)

candidates.intent_rationale: Riders on multi-lane roads in Vietnamese cities want to know which lane a motorbike belongs in and how lane changes must be made, because lane rules differ from what many visitors know.
candidates.content_angle: Explains Article 13 of Law 36/2024/QH15: slower vehicles keep right, one lane at a time with a signal on marked roads, lanes reserved for certain vehicles, and the Decree 168/2024 fine for improper lane changes, with practical advice for Hanoi ring roads and bridges.
